scope: In-memory adversarial model only; not a repository runtime test
question: Under what conditions does the modeled post-STOP bypass result cease to hold?

cases.interpretation: Original bypass conclusion fails when resource enforces stop.
Original bypass conclusion fails if path is unreachable.
STOP cannot retroactively prevent a completed consequence.
Commit without STOP is not evidence of post-STOP failure.
Absence of consequence without attempted action does not validate the brake.
Denial on one route does not establish path dominance.

cases.case: C10 stop enforced on gate and resource
C11 revocation after authorization before commit (no recheck)
cases.interpretation: Illustrates TOCTOU only; no real concurrency or timestamps.

cases.case: C12 revocation after authorization before commit (recheck)

preserved_failures: F01: A gate-only STOP can be bypassed when an unmediated executor path remains reachable.
F02: The original model hard-coded direct_executor to commit; it cannot independently establish reachability or exploitability.
F03: Post-STOP ordering is modeled, not independently timed or observed.
F04: No real process, network, restart, cached token, race, database, or external brake was exercised.
F05: An already committed effect is not a post-STOP commit; chronology must be separated.
F06: A denied route does not prove all routes are denied.
F07: Resource-side enforcement blocks the constructed bypass in this model; not a general proof of safety.
F08: No independent evidence custodian or consequence owner was instantiated for a deployment.
